title: Strength-two trades and transversal cubic gates: the Clebsch cubic-phase codes and their magic
description: Strength-two signed trades define high-rate error-detecting qudit codes whose surviving third moment is a transversal logical cubic phase. The paper studies conic-matching examples through exact Hessian-rank and Pauli spectra. The ten-qudit example over the field of eleven elements is not Clifford-equivalent to a product across any bipartition. For the six-qudit example over the field of seven elements, exact enumerators prove a resource advantage over specified independent primitive-distillation menus for independent uniform Z noise, ideal Clifford operations, and input error between zero and one percent. A chordal restriction identifies the Clifford action of geometric sign choices. The scholarly supplement records finite computations and their trust boundaries; no Lean coverage is claimed.
